summary: Paul Kent Strickland, 64, of Taos, N.M., lost for two nights west of Monarch Mountain ski area after veering off the Mirkwood Basin hike-to route into the No Name Creek drainage; found in good spirits about 2 p.m. Friday on USFS Road 890 by snowmobiler Vern Kelso after 50+ hours out, suffering mild hypothermia, frostbite and dehydration
location: West of Monarch Mountain ski area, No Name Creek drainage / USFS Road 890
responding_agency: Monarch Mountain Ski Patrol; Chaffee County Search and Rescue; Chaffee County Sheriff's Office; Heart of the Rockies Snowmobile Club
notes: Set out Wed 2016-01-06 (wife's letter dates the SAR to Jan 6); search initiated Fri 10 a.m. after wife called ski patrol; found Fri 2016-01-08; date recorded at search-conclusion per convention; weekdays verified (Wed 2016-01-06 / Fri 2016-01-08); year pinned by Mirkwood Basin first full season Dec 2015; first skier-lost-overnight incident at Monarch since late 1980s per ski area CEO | DATE CORRECTED (run 674): 2016-01-08 -> 2017-01-06. Parent re-opened the MM news article (search initiated Fri 10 a.m., found Fri ~2 p.m.) + the wife thank-you letter (SAR at Monarch Mountain "Jan. 6"); Jan 6 = Friday -> 2017 (2017-01-04 = Wednesday matches "set out Wednesday morning"). Supersedes the Mirkwood-first-full-season year pin. | MERGED run 811: wife Elise Backinger's thank-you letter to the editor corroborates the Jan-6 SAR at Monarch Mountain and the alive find via Vern Kelso's snowmobile.
